messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: [INCIDENT] high NXDOMAIN/timeout rate from EU resolvers detected for geo-redwood.example.com. Affects EU region customers. Pager to oncall-sre.

nora: got it, paging in. i'm oncall for SRE. kicking off triage — sam you free?

sam: i'm in. seeing spike in resolver timeouts from Cloudflare EU and occasional mismatched answers from Route53. Confirming customer impact.

eli: support dashboard shows ~12% of requests returning 5xx from our edge gateway for EU; most times correlating with DNS lookup failures. some customers report 502 from our API layer.

maya: fielding inbound tickets — two paying customers flagged timeouts in app during 09:18-09:25 UTC. they saw quick retries then recovered.

jordan: quick check: our geoDNS health probes show intermittent failures to primary CF resolver IPs from eu-west probes. Route53 answers are OK but TTLs are long (300s).

nora: can we fail traffic to secondary geoDNS pool? what's the safe playbook?

sam: propose temporary routing policy: shift 30% to fallback pool in eu-west-2, monitor error delta. if errors drop => continue, if not => full failover.

eli: +1. also recommend enabling aggressive caching in frontend for 30s to reduce repeated lookups during propagation.

lina: starting canary reroute now via infra tool. command:```bash
redwood-geoctl change-policy --name geo-redwood --from primary-eu --to fallback-eu --percent 30 --note "auto-mitigate-resolver-fail-1765432100"
```

support-bot: noted. Support ticket #4528 linked. Customers impacted: AcmeCorp, BetaSaaS. Sending update to both.

sam: can we also add a DNS provider-level failover to Route53 for critical records? If CF resolvers keep flaking, we should reduce dependency on one resolver pool.

jordan: Route53 is already a secondary zone for some records but not all. need a small change batch to create health-check-based failover for `api.eu.redwood.example.com`.

maya: running status page update draft: "We are investigating increased DNS resolver errors affecting EU traffic; mitigation in progress (traffic reroute). Some customers may experience brief errors or elevated latency." want to post?

nora: post it. tag customers via workspace.

sam: monitoring metrics — after 30% shift, DNS errors dropped to ~5% and gateway 5xx fell to ~3%. Looks promising.

eli: good. step: increase shift to 80% over next 3 minutes if stable.

lina: increasing to 80% now.```bash
redwood-geoctl change-policy --name geo-redwood --to fallback-eu --percent 80 --wait 180
```

incbot: by the way, Cloudflare status API shows partial outage for EU resolver probes: https://status.cloudflare.com/ (link)

sam: that explains it. still seeing occasional mismatched answers when CF returns SERVFAIL and Route53 returns valid answer — caching differences + TTL causing transient mismatch.

jordan: to speed recovery, i'm lowering TTL for `api.eu.redwood.example.com` from 300 -> 60 on Route53 for the critical record. change script:```json
{
  "Comment": "reduce TTL for failover",
  "Changes": [{"Action": "UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "api.eu.redwood.example.com.","Type": "A","TTL": 60,"ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "54.12.34.56"}]}}]
}
```

maya: support notified customers with workaround: retry/backoff for client-side; recommend edge caching enabled. will escalate to accounts for high-value customers.

nora: good. keep monitoring. tagging eng-runtime for potential rate-limit work around if we see DNS-lookups spike CPU on edge gateways.

eli: alert: one of our EU edge nodes still showing DNS resolution error bursts even after failover. investigating dnsmasq cache saturation.

sam: try clearing local resolver cache on that node and restarting resolver service. lina can you run:```bash
sudo systemctl restart redwood-dns-resolver || sudo pkill -HUP dnsmasq
```

lina: restart done on eu-edge-07. DNS lookup error rate on that host dropped to baseline.

incbot: :white_check_mark: mitigation progress: traffic shifted to fallback pool, TTL lowered, resolver restarts applied. Continue monitoring for 30m.

jordan: ops note: we still have a Route53 propagation window ~2-5 minutes per client depending on intermediate caches. expect some scattered errors until fully propagated.

maya: posting customer update: "Mitigation in place — traffic routed to fallback cluster, we restarted resolvers on affected nodes, and lowered DNS TTLs. We're monitoring and will update when fully recovered."

support-bot: sent updates to affected customers. ticket #4528 updated, ETA for next update 15m.

nora: moving to handoff. sam stay with watch, i'll do next-oncall summary at +30. primary follow-ups: postmortem, add active CF resolver probes, automate TTL drop for future failovers, document runbook steps.

sam: ack. i'll own runbook PR and probes.

eli: i'll produce quick incident timeline for postmortem.

lina: will add resolver cache health metrics to dashboard and set alert threshold.

incbot: incident severity downgraded to SEV2 at 09:55 UTC. final check: error rates down to normal and customers reporting recovery. :tada:

nora: thanks team. creating incident record and assigning postmortem to sam/eli. closing thread after handoff. :white_check_mark:
